artifact.sourceExcerpt: Ἡροδότου Ἁλικαρνησσέος ἱστορίης ἀπόδεξις ἥδε, ὡς μήτε τὰ γενόμενα ἐξ ἀνθρώπων τῷ χρόνῳ ἐξίτηλα γένηται, μήτε ἔργα μεγάλα τε καὶ θωμαστά, τὰ μὲν Ἕλλησι τὰ δὲ βαρβάροισι ἀποδεχθέντα, ἀκλεᾶ γένηται, τά τε ἄλλα καὶ διʼ ἣν αἰτίην ἐπολέμησαν ἀλλήλοισι.
artifact.literalTranslation: This is the presentation of the inquiry of Herodotus of Halicarnassus, so that neither the things that have come to be from human beings may become faded away by time, nor great and wondrous deeds, some displayed by Greeks and others by foreigners, may become without glory, and also, among other things, the cause for which they fought one another.
artifact.readerTranslation: Here Herodotus of Halicarnassus sets out his inquiry: so that human events will not be erased by time, so that the great and astonishing deeds of Greeks and non-Greeks alike will not lose their fame, and so that the cause of their war with one another may be known.

preposition plus accusative singular feminine relative phrase

illustrationPromptSeed.style: Ionian field notebook: reed-pen linework, sea-weathered blues, red-figure silhouette accents, clear map labels, consistent traveler-narrator presence.
illustrationPromptSeed.prompt: Opening page for Herodotus's inquiry: a seated Ionian recorder from Halicarnassus unfurls a map between Greek and Persian worlds, with small margin vignettes of ships, cities, and opposing armies. Preserve a documentary notebook feel, use restrained sea-blue washes and red-figure accents, no modern clothing, no fantasy effects.

uncertainties: `ἀπόδεξις` can be rendered as display, publication, or presentation; `sets out` was chosen for the reader version.
`βαρβάροισι` is translated as `non-Greeks` in the reader version to avoid importing a modern pejorative tone.
The chunk boundary is intentionally smaller than the whole 0.1% span for a tiny kickoff sample.
